subject: Pilot access blocked by dev-queue stall — request for short extension & credits
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@opsly.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot access + short runway — Opsly / Redwood

Hi Jordan,

Quick note from the Opsly engineering team — we hit a blocker while wiring the webhook handler to your SDK. The queue consumer on our side is throttling due to a schema mismatch that only shows up under higher parallelism; it prevents us from completing the connector tests.

This means our pilot (DL-2983) can't move to the demo stage this week as planned. We were counting on the current sandbox credits and the standard 14-day pilot window to finish the integration, but with the queue stall we need a little breathing room.

Ask: could Redwood provide a short runway extension (2–3 weeks) and a sandbox top-up so our engineers can run repeated integration passes without hitting token limits? If helpful I can share logs and reproduce steps — attaching a short runbook from our side.

Appreciate any help — we really like the performance numbers so far and want to keep momentum.

Samir
VP of Engineering, Opsly
attachments: opsly_runbook_v1.pdf

----
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@opsly.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot access + short runway — Opsly / Redwood

Samir — thanks for flagging and for the context.

Really sorry to hear about the queue issue; we want to keep this pilot moving. I’ve looped in Dev (infra/SDK) and Laura (sales lead) to evaluate a short runway and credit top-up. To speed things up, can you send the minimal repro and the two most recent error traces?

Proposed immediate resolution (tentative):
- 2-week pilot extension
- 20k sandbox credit top-up to cover repeated integration runs

If engineering says they need more time/credits we’ll escalate for manager sign-off. We’ll confirm by EOD tomorrow.

—Jordan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T10:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot access + short runway — Opsly / Redwood

Thanks for the heads up. I pulled the logs Samir shared (opsly_runbook_v1.pdf + traces) and reproduced the failure locally. Summary: under higher concurrency the client is sending a deprecated metadata field that causes our consumer to drop some messages; there’s an easy server-side guard we can patch in ~4–6 hours, but Opsly will need to re-run the connector tests across multiple scaling profiles to validate.

Impact estimate:
- Dev work: ~0.5 day to patch + 1 day for Opsly to re-run full regression.
- Risk: if we need to triage additional schema cases, the cycle can stretch to ~10 business days.

Recommendation: give the customer a 3-week window and a 30k credit top-up to avoid repeated interruptions while they iterate. I attached a short impact calc showing token burn estimates for the test matrix (runway_impact_calc.xlsx).

If approved I’ll prepare a prioritized patch and a verification checklist they can run against staging.

Attachments: integration_error_log.txt, runway_impact_calc.xlsx

—Dev
Principal Engineer, Infrastructure

On Tue, May 2, 2027 at 9:07 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:

Date: 2027-05-04T08:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot access + short runway — Opsly / Redwood

Jordan / Dev — thanks for the quick analysis. I’m comfortable approving a limited runway and credit top-up to keep momentum, with two stipulations:

1) Opsly agrees to a 3-week extension from the original pilot end date and signs a short mutual action plan (MAP) listing the steps and success criteria. We should capture that MAP in Drive and attach to the deal.
2) The credit top-up is a one-time sandbox supplement of 25,000 tokens; any additional needs beyond that require commercial review.

Rationale: 25k hits the middle ground between the engineering ask and standard pilot generosity. If Dev’s verification checklist shows additional risk we can fast-track a second review, but I want to keep approvals from stretching.

Please confirm I should send the formal approval note and generate the DocuSign amendment. Jordan — once you confirm I’ll route the approval through our finance ops and mark the deal stage in HubSpot.

—Laura
Sales Director, Redwood Inference

Samir — good news. We can support Opsly with a short runway to finish validation. Summary of what we’re providing:

Conditions:
- Please fill out the one-page MAP (link below) with target test cases and expected pass criteria.

Samir, confirm you received this and whether Opsly can target May 12 for the first verification run.
